logline.hi: Posting के छठे हफ़्ते में Sub-Inspector नंदिनी जोशी को पता चलता है कि इमलीपुर में कोई उसके थाने क्यों नहीं आता: railway line के उस पार, बंद पड़े talkies में, एक आदमी पूरी वर्दी पहनकर दूसरा थाना चला रहा है, और उससे अच्छा चला रहा है। Order है कि कल दस बजे से पहले उसे arrest करो। पर कस्बे के दबंग भैयाजी के ख़िलाफ़ इकलौता case उसी नक़ली Inspector की files में है, और भैयाजी उसे अपना ख़रीदा हुआ अफ़सर समझते हैं।
logline.en: Six weeks into her first posting, Sub-Inspector Nandini Joshi finds out why nobody in Imlipur brings a complaint to her thana: across the railway line, in a shut-down cinema, a man in a too-perfect uniform runs a second police station, and runs it better. Her orders are to arrest him before ten tomorrow. But the only case against the town's strongman is in the fake inspector's files, and the strongman thinks he is the one officer he has bought.

premise: Imlipur is a small fictional town cut in two by a railway line. Its real thana has not registered an FIR in two years and has a zero-crime shield to show for it; every complaint its SHO refused walked across the line to the shut Roopam Talkies, where Sudhir Nirala, who failed the police entrance nine times, runs a thana of his own with tokens, stamps and perfect registers. Sub-Inspector Nandini Joshi, six weeks into her first posting, finds it, reports it up the line and is ordered to have him in her lockup before the DSP's press conference at ten the next morning. In his files she finds thirty complaints against the strongman Bhaiyaji, each one turned away by her own thana, and two years of Bhaiyaji's bribes sealed and dated as case property. That night Bhaiyaji calls his 'Inspector साहब' to the godown at midnight to stamp a slip while eight hundred sacks of ration grain leave town, and nobody knows what her own SHO told Bhaiyaji on the phone that evening. By eleven she has to choose: cuff a frightened man who cannot defend himself, or let him be a policeman for one more night.
tone: A warm small-town caper with real stakes. The comedy is deadpan and comes from procedure taken seriously by the one man with no right to it: tokens, stamps, receipts, a lockup that is a ticket booth. Nobody mugs and nobody is a fool; Nirala means every word, which is why he is funny. The stakes are real: stolen ration grain, a bought SHO, an unarmed man walking into a godown, an officer's badge. No violence on screen, no gore, no slapstick. How dark: one frightened man and one cornered SHO, never more. Reference feel: the gentle moral comedy of small-town Hindi films, played with a thriller's clock. No narrator anywhere; picture, sound and dialogue carry every fact.

About 12:10 a.m.: the truck passes the crossing on Tripathi's signature (s2a01).

Some days later: the bail hearing (s2b03). Some weeks later: the help desk (s2b03 final image); both trials are still a month away.

characters.addressed_as: 'Madam' by everyone; 'SI Joshi' or 'Joshi' by the DSP; 'Joshi' by Tripathi when angry.
characters.bio: Academy topper on her first posting, second-in-command at the Imlipur thana for six weeks. Exact, impatient and privately bored: she has not written one FIR since she arrived. She has put in her own application for a transfer to the city. She is the one who reports the fake thana up the line, which is what starts the clock.
characters.want: To do the job she was trained for, by the book. At the start that means getting out of Imlipur; by the question it means deciding what the book is for.
characters.secret: Her transfer application, six weeks into a first posting, is her own doing and is pending with the DSP. Pushpa says it aloud in s2e01. It is never mentioned in the s2e03 choice scene, on the question card, on the ballot or in either glimpse. In branch A she withdraws it herself in s2a03. In branch B it is moot and is not mentioned again.
characters.look: Indian woman, 28, tall (about 170 cm), lean, very straight-backed, long neck. Medium-brown skin, oval face, straight thick black eyebrows, level dark-brown eyes, a firm mouth that rarely smiles. Black hair with a clean centre parting pulled into a low ponytail that reaches her shoulder blades; no fringe, no loose strands. No make-up, no bindi, no jewellery, no watch. PERIOD 1 (every episode except the last image of branch B): the approved force uniform, crisp and new: sandy khaki shirt with a pointed collar and two buttoned chest pockets, full sleeves buttoned at the wrist, sharp pressed creases; dark teal epaulettes with TWO off-white bars each; white lantern on a round teal patch on each upper sleeve; khaki trousers; black belt with a black handcuff pouch on her right hip; black shoes; a blue ballpoint pen clipped in her left chest pocket. No cap, no name tag, no stars. She carries a cherry-red open-face scooter helmet under her left arm whenever she is outdoors or has just arrived (it sits on a desk or bench otherwise). PERIOD 2 (s2b03 final image only): a plain mustard-yellow cotton kurta with elbow-length sleeves over off-white trousers, the same low ponytail, the same blue pen now tucked behind her right ear. From the middle of s2b01 to the end of s2b02 Nirala's brass medal is in her left chest pocket (out of sight). In s2a02 her LEFT wrist is handcuffed to Nirala's RIGHT wrist.
characters.silhouette: Tallest woman in the series: a straight vertical line with a low ponytail and a round helmet under one arm.
characters.voice_note: Female, late twenties, clear mid-range voice. Educated small-city north-Indian Hindi with crisp English police and office words; the most English-mixed speaker in the cast. Quick, clipped, finishes other people's sentences. Under pressure she gets quieter, slower and more exact, never louder. Dry, not sarcastic. The same actor in both languages.

voice_by_language.hi: Hinglish: Hindi grammar with English nouns and verbs ('arrest', 'register', 'handover', 'order'). Short lines. Says 'निराला जी', 'SHO साहब', 'DSP साहब', 'पुष्पा जी'.
voice_by_language.en: Indian English, neutral educated accent (no British or American colour). Keeps 'madam', 'thana', 'FIR', 'lockup', 'ji'. Same clip and dryness.

sample_line.hi: मैं इस इलाके की SI हूँ। और ये थाना मेरे record में है ही नहीं।
sample_line.en: I am the SI for this area. And this thana is not in my records at all.

characters.addressed_as: 'निराला जी' by the town, Nandini and Pushpa. 'Inspector साहब' ONLY in Bhaiyaji's mouth (set up in s2e02). Nobody else ever calls him Inspector.
characters.bio: Former booking clerk of Roopam Talkies, which is why he has its keys, its ticket booth and its habit of tokens. He sat the police entrance nine times and failed the physical each time by one centimetre of chest. When the talkies shut two years ago he stitched himself a uniform and opened a thana in the lobby. He takes complaints, settles small disputes, issues stamped receipts and keeps better registers than any real thana. He has no power to act against Bhaiyaji, so he has done the one thing he can: written everything down, and sealed every bribe Bhaiyaji paid him as case property, with the note numbers.
characters.want: To hand his files to a real officer before he is taken away: 'charge handover'. Under that, to have been, once, a policeman.
characters.secret: His revolver is carved from teak and has never left its holster; he cannot defend himself and he is frightened of Bhaiyaji. He hides this from the whole town. It surfaces in s2e03, played straight.
characters.look: Indian man, 40, slight and short (about 160 cm), narrow sloping shoulders, thin neck, a chest that does not fill a shirt. Light-brown skin, long narrow face, large earnest eyes, a neat black pencil moustache, clean-shaven chin. PERIOD 1 (everything except the last two images of branch B): a home-stitched copy of the force uniform, over-starched and ONE SIZE TOO BIG: the shoulder seams droop past his shoulders, the sleeves end at his knuckles, the collar stands away from his neck, the trousers are belted high with the tail of the black belt hanging loose. Teal epaulettes with three off-white bars; lantern sleeve patches. THE ONLY PEAKED CAP IN THE SERIES: a khaki peaked cap with a teal band and a shiny black peak, no badge, worn dead level and never taken off. ONE THING TOO MANY: a single home-made medal pinned above his left chest pocket: a blank brass-yellow disc as wide as his palm hanging from a broad maroon-and-off-white striped ribbon; no text, no emblem. A brown leather holster with a buttoned flap on his right hip holds the wooden revolver. A rubber stamp and a small tin ink pad live in his right trouser pocket. PERIOD 1b (branch B only, from s2b01 b2 to the end of s2b02): the same uniform after Nandini has dressed him: NO MEDAL, sleeve cuffs folded back so his hands show, the belt pulled tight with its tail tucked in, the shoulder seams squared; cap, holster and moustache unchanged. S6 decides whether this needs its own drawing. PERIOD 2 (s2b03): in court the cap is off for the first time in the series and lies on the evidence table: flat, neatly side-parted black hair pressed down by years under a cap; in the final image he wears a plain white half-sleeve shirt, grey trousers and the same moustache, no cap, no medal. Medal: on his chest from s2e01; in branch B Nandini unpins it in s2b01 and it is next seen on the evidence table and then as a paperweight on the help desk. Revolver: holstered until s2e03; in branch A sealed as case property in s2a01; in branch B holstered in s2b01, taken by Bhaiyaji in s2b02, on the evidence table in s2b03.
characters.silhouette: The smallest man in the series under the only peaked cap: a level cap, drooping shoulders, sleeves over his hands, one big disc on his chest.
characters.voice_note: Male, forty, light careful tenor. Small-town north-Indian Hindi in an official register: complete sentences, passive constructions ('shutter गिरा दिया गया है'), English police terms pronounced with great care. Unhurried, courteous, never raises his voice, never jokes: the comedy is that he means it. Under pressure he becomes more formal and quieter, and his sentences get shorter. Frightened is a thin, steady voice, not a stammer. The same actor in both languages.

voice_by_language.hi: Hindi-heavy with borrowed procedure words ('complaint', 'receipt', 'case property', 'charge handover', 'seizure memo'). Says 'madam' at the end of sentences.
voice_by_language.en: Careful, slightly old-fashioned Indian English, as learnt from manuals: 'kindly', 'the same', 'as per'. No contractions when nervous.

sample_line.hi: बैठिए madam। पहले चाय, फिर complaint।
sample_line.en: Please sit, madam. First tea, then complaint.

characters.addressed_as: 'SHO साहब' by his staff; 'त्रिपाठी जी' by Bhaiyaji and the DSP. Never a bare 'साहब'.
characters.bio: The real SHO, four years from retirement. He has not registered an FIR in two years, and the zero-crime shield on his wall is the result. Bhaiyaji pays him to turn complaints away. He found out long ago where the people he refused were going and said nothing to anyone: exposing the fake thana would expose how he got his shield.
characters.want: A quiet road to his pension, with the shield on the wall and the almirah locked.
characters.secret: He has known about the fake thana for two years and told neither the department nor Bhaiyaji. Pushpa says so in s2e02. When Nandini reports it, the secret is about to come out in the worst way, so at the end of s2e02 he tells Bhaiyaji first. What he says is heard by nobody. The same evening, off screen, he signs and stamps the movement slip for the midnight truck himself; this is true in both branches and is first seen in s2a01 b6 (branch A) or heard in s2b01 b9 (branch B).
characters.look: Indian man, 56, large, heavy and slow, about 175 cm, a big soft belly straining his shirt. Warm-brown skin, bald dome with a fringe of grey hair at the sides, heavy jowls, clean-shaven, half-closed sleepy eyes. Approved force uniform worn slack: khaki half-sleeve shirt with the top two buttons open over a white vest, teal epaulettes with three off-white bars, lantern sleeve patches, khaki trousers. A red-and-white checked gamchha always over his LEFT shoulder. ALWAYS EATING: a paper cone of roasted peanuts in his left hand, shells on whatever surface is near him. No cap. One outfit throughout.
characters.silhouette: The widest shape in the series: a bald dome, a cloth over one shoulder, a paper cone in one hand.
characters.voice_note: Male, mid-fifties, deep, slow, comfortable baritone, often speaking round a mouthful. Eastern-UP small-town Hindi, very little English beyond 'FIR', 'zero crime', 'file'. Avuncular and lazy; he ends arguments by offering food. Under pressure he does not shout: he stops chewing, goes flat and low, and then blames someone. The same actor in both languages.

voice_by_language.en: Slow Indian English with Hindi fillers kept ('arre madam', 'chhodiye'); never crisp.

sample_line.hi: जहाँ complaint नहीं, वहाँ crime नहीं, madam। मूँगफली लीजिए।
sample_line.en: No complaint, no crime, madam. Have some peanuts.

characters.addressed_as: 'भैयाजी' by everyone, including the police. His full name is spoken only when it is read into an FIR, a memo or a court order.
characters.bio: Runs the ration godown and most of Imlipur. He diverts ration grain and squeezes those who complain. He pays Tripathi to refuse complaints and, for two years, has also paid the 'new outpost' across the line, which costs less and never acts. He has never doubted it: the SHO never objected to it.
characters.want: Eight hundred sacks out of town tonight, and thirty complaints that stay asleep in a file.
characters.secret: From about 7 p.m. on the night of the story he knows the Inspector is a fake, because Tripathi told him, and he already holds the movement slip signed and stamped by Tripathi. So the midnight invitation is not for a stamp: it is for Nirala. The viewer does not know either fact at the choice. Branch B: Nirala reads the SHO's signature off the slip aloud (s2b01 b9) and Bhaiyaji laughs and says it (b10). Branch A: Nandini reads the signature at the crossing (s2a01 b6) and the two of them infer the rest from the slip (s2a01 b8); it is never confirmed.
characters.look: Indian man, 45, broad and solid, about 178 cm, thick neck, big square hands. Brown skin, thick black hair combed straight back, a full black moustache, an unhurried closed-lip smile that is his resting face. A spotless white cotton kurta with the sleeves pushed up his forearms over white pyjama trousers; brown leather sandals. A heavy gold watch on his LEFT wrist. Dark sunglasses pushed up on top of his head, never over his eyes, with two exceptions: in s2a03 b4 they slide down onto his nose when his name is read out, and in s2b03 b2 and b6 they are folded in his hand. A fat ring of godown keys hooked on his RIGHT index finger, which he lets swing. No religious marks, no party colours, no scarf. One outfit throughout.
characters.silhouette: A broad white block with sunglasses on its head and a bunch of keys hanging from one finger.
characters.voice_note: Male, mid-forties, warm, low, smiling voice. Small-town north-Indian Hindi, courteous to the point of menace; he never threatens and never hurries, and he laughs before he says the worst thing. Under pressure the smile leaves the voice and nothing replaces it: flat and quiet. The same actor in both languages.

voice_by_language.hi: Hindi-heavy, hospitable ('आइए, आइए'), English only for 'Inspector', 'slip', 'godown', 'truck'.
voice_by_language.en: Soft, hospitable Indian English; keeps 'Inspector sahab', 'Tripathi ji', 'aaiye'.

characters.addressed_as: 'पुष्पा जी' by Nandini and Nirala; 'Head Constable' by the DSP.
characters.bio: Twenty-six years at the Imlipur thana. She knits through every shift and has watched every complaint come in and be sent away. She knows where everything is and has waited years for an officer to ask.
characters.want: One officer who will write things down. Then she will hand over everything she has kept.
characters.secret: Two. She is the one who quietly told every complainant Tripathi refused to go across the line to the talkies; she says so in s2e02. And she has a second key to the SHO's locked almirah, where the FIR register sits, on a loop of wool in her cardigan pocket; it surfaces in s2a01 in branch A and is not used in branch B.
characters.look: Indian woman, 50, short (about 152 cm) and solid, round shoulders, strong forearms. Wheat-brown skin, round face, sharp small eyes over round steel-rimmed spectacles worn low on her nose. Grey-streaked black hair in a tight high bun with TWO STEEL KNITTING NEEDLES pushed through it in a cross. Approved force uniform: khaki full-sleeve shirt, teal epaulettes with ONE off-white bar, lantern sleeve patches, khaki trousers, black shoes. Over it, always, a hand-knitted plum-purple cardigan, open at the front, with two sagging pockets; a ball of orange wool shows in the right pocket. A cloth knitting bag over her left shoulder outdoors. No cap. One outfit throughout.
characters.silhouette: Short and square, a bun with two crossed needles, a cardigan over the uniform.
characters.voice_note: Female, fifty, low, dry, even alto. Small-town Hindi, plain and economical; she says the important thing in the fewest words and then goes back to her knitting. Never surprised. Under pressure she gets slower and more exact, and her knitting stops. Warmth shows only as dryness. The same actor in both languages.

voice_by_language.hi: Hindi-heavy; English only for ranks and 'FIR', 'call', 'phone'. Always 'madam', 'SHO साहब', 'निराला जी'.
voice_by_language.en: Plain, unhurried Indian English; short sentences; keeps 'madam', 'SHO sahab', 'Nirala ji'.

sample_line.hi: SHO साहब जिसे लौटाते थे, उसे line के पार मैं भेजती थी, madam।
sample_line.en: Whoever SHO sahab turned away, I sent across the line, madam.

characters.addressed_as: 'DSP साहब' by everyone. Never 'साहब' or 'बड़े साहब' alone.
characters.bio: The sub-division's DSP. Brisk, image-minded, not corrupt: he likes a clean district and a good headline. Tomorrow at ten he holds a press conference at the Imlipur thana for its second zero-crime year, and he wants the fake thana to be a finished arrest before then, not a question.
characters.want: Nothing untidy in front of microphones.
characters.secret: None. He does not know what his zero-crime thana is made of. He finds out in s2a03 (branch A) or by phone in s2b02 (branch B).
characters.look: Indian man, 48, tall (about 182 cm) and lean, upright, quick. Brown skin, short silver-grey hair with a side parting, a trimmed grey moustache, rimless rectangular spectacles. Approved force uniform, sharply pressed: khaki full-sleeve shirt, teal epaulettes each carrying ONE BROAD off-white band (the senior mark of this fictional force; no bars, no stars), lantern sleeve patches, khaki trousers, a polished brown belt, a slim brown leather cane tucked under his LEFT arm. No cap. On screen only in branch A (last beat of s2a02 and all of s2a03); a phone voice in s2e01, s2e03 and s2b02.
characters.silhouette: The tallest, thinnest uniform: spectacles, a cane under one arm.
characters.voice_note: Male, late forties, bright, quick, clipped baritone; the voice of a man who is always half addressing the press. City Hindi with a lot of English. Impatient, cuts people off, gives orders as times and places. On the phone he is heard through a phone filter and must stay intelligible. Under pressure he pauses once, then pivots smoothly. The same actor in both languages.

voice_by_language.hi: Most English-heavy after Nandini: 'press conference', 'arrest', 'information', 'force'. Says 'SI Joshi', 'त्रिपाठी जी'.
voice_by_language.en: Fluent officer's Indian English, brisk; no British or American colour.

sample_line.hi: कल दस बजे मेरी press conference है, SI Joshi। उससे पहले वो आदमी lockup में चाहिए।
sample_line.en: My press conference is at ten tomorrow, SI Joshi. I want that man in the lockup before it.
