length_budget.ceiling: Each episode is writable at about 120 spoken seconds and no more than about 135 (the D-005 ceiling). There is no cap on beat count: beats do not cost time, dialogue does.
length_budget.working_measure: PROVISIONAL, until a speech rate is measured: key lines at or under about 950 characters an episode, so a finished script stays near 1,050. s2e03 may run to about 1,050 in key lines, because nearly every line in it is one.
length_budget.showrunner_hand_estimate_after_cuts: By eye, not counted by a tool, speaker labels excluded, likely error ten per cent either way: s2e01 about 950, s2e02 about 945, s2e03 about 1,035, s2a01 about 930, s2a02 about 945, s2a03 about 950, s2b01 about 680, s2b02 about 950, s2b03 about 945. Several sit on the line. The first agent with a shell must count them; if an episode is over, the writer trims connective lines first and unprotected key lines second.
length_budget.protected_from_cuts: Every line D-006 changed or added; s2e03 b4 to b10; every spoken episode ending and both glimpse endings; the say-it-aloud plant in s2e02 b4.
length_budget.may_be_restored: If the first measured voice takes run at 11 characters a second or faster, the showrunner may restore lines cut for length. Cut from key lines in this revision: s2e01 b6 (that the talkies has been shut two years), b7 ('छह हफ़्ते में ही?'), b10 (the index); s2e02 b1 ('कल दस बजे तक का वक़्त दीजिए'), b3 (the register will say whose cycle it is), b5 (the section-number correction), b8 ('चौबीस महीने'), b11 (Tripathi sending Pushpa for tea, now action only); s2e03 b3 (the carbon copies; D-006 says these stay cut); s2a02 b9 ('वही काफ़ी है'); s2a03 b6 (the note numbers), b8 ('तीस FIR, DSP साहब'); s2b02 b7 (the split count), b9 ('बिना बुलाए'); s2b03 b5 ('DSP साहब का नहीं'), b6 (the seizure-memo line), b10 (the medal line), b11 (where FIRs are now written).

notes: One-word turns and lines that open on an ellipsis get a carrier word or extra takes, decided line by line by the writer and the voice director. This is not a rule: nothing measured supports one.
s2e03 b4 may take one clause on why Pushpa comes so late (she heard the call at seven and arrives after half past ten), if there is room.

s2e03 b5, optional, only if the measured budget allows: nirala 'ना गया, तो वो यहाँ आएँगे, madam।' It says why doing neither is not a third option. It is not in the key lines because s2e03 is already at its limit by estimate.

s2b01 b9 may play over two or three insert stills from inside the godown, with no faces (a sack's stencil patch, the weighing scale, the pink slip in a hand), if S7 finds fifty seconds of two listeners at the stall too static.

A phone-filtered line never sits directly on a loud effect. This matters most for s2b01 b8 (the shutter rattle must die a full second before Nirala's line), s2b01 b10 (the laugh) and s2e03 b6 (the DSP).

s2b01 b8: Nirala's line is full voice and addressed to Bhaiyaji. He never says 'madam' while the call is open inside the godown; the danger word in s2b02 b3 is said after the call is dead, under his breath.

s2e03 b6 and s2b02 b10 are a pair: the DSP's 'नक़ली थाने के phone पर सुनी बात' is answered by her 'अब बात नक़ली थाने के phone की नहीं है'. Keep the echo. He never withdraws 'उसी FIR में उसका नाम होगा'.
s2a01 b9 says 'सुबह दस बजे', not 'कल': it is past midnight when Nirala says it.
s2a02 b10: the voice turns the handcuffs against Nirala; Nandini answers with 'हथकड़ी मेरी है'. It is her door. Nirala says nothing in this beat.
The antagonist's full name, बलराम ठाकुर, is spoken only when read into a record: s2a03 b4, s2b02 b6, s2b03 b8. Everywhere else he is 'भैयाजी'.

Open point for the writer of s2b03, raised by the showrunner and not ruled on: in b10 the medal is still on the evidence table, and in the final image, weeks later and with both trials pending, it is a paperweight on the help desk. Both images are approved and closed. If the writer wants to cover the gap, one clause is enough; do not move either image.

content_notes: Fictional police force and insignia (the lantern force from the proof scene); no national flag or emblem; no portraits; no real people.
